templates.text: Barely moving — still folded, still quiet, breathing shallow but steady.
Eyes half-open, body limp and warm, only the faintest chest rise visible.
Motionless except for the tiniest lip tremble and a slow blink.
So still that only the pulse at the fontanelle proved anything at all.
Limbs remained softly curled, no startle, only a faint nasal flaring with each breath.
The newborn lay in a quiet repose, a single slow hand movement the only sign of life.
A profound stillness, broken only by the gentle, rhythmic parting of the lips.
Eyes closed, body yielding to the mattress, breath a whisper against the cheek.
Muscle tone was minimal, the infant's form a soft weight, respiration barely stirring the air.
The chest rose and fell in shallow, almost imperceptible waves beneath still hands.
A delayed, weak rooting reflex after {seconds} seconds of complete motionlessness.
Pale eyelids fluttered once, then settled, the body a landscape of profound calm.
Only the subtle tremor of an outstretched finger betrayed the quiet internal shift.
Respiration was silent and slow, the abdomen doing the faintest work of breathing.
The baby lay supine, arms adducted, in a state of drowsy, postural inertia.
A sigh, more felt than heard, preceded a long pause before the next breath.
Skin-to-skin warmth was met with a slow, melting relaxation into the caregiver's chest.
The Moro reflex was absent; the limbs simply remained where they were placed.
Eyes opened to a slit, gazed vaguely, then closed again with a long exhalation.
The fontanelle pulsed softly under a tranquil brow, all other movement suspended.
A faint, damp curl of hair was the only thing that moved in the still air.
Breathing was so shallow the stethoscope bell had to be held with utmost stillness.
The grasp reflex was a ghost of pressure, released almost as soon as it was felt.
Lips pursed in a silent, sleepy suckle, then fell slack against the gums.
The infant's stillness was so complete it seemed a continuation of the womb.
A single tear welled in the corner of a closed eye, tracing a slow path downward.
The torso was warm and soft, rising in a slow cadence of {seconds}-second intervals.
No cry, just the wet sound of a tongue separating from the palate once, softly.
The baby's hand lay open, palm up, fingers slightly curled in passive flexion.
A minimal response to light: pupils constricted slightly, then dilation returned.
The head lolled to the side, supported only by the yielding surface beneath.
Breath formed a tiny, transient fog on the cool surface of the warming bed.
All energy seemed conserved, focused inward on the task of circulation and breath.
A subtle startle at a sudden sound resolved into a deeper, more settled stillness.
A faint, rhythmic pursing of the lips accompanied each shallow, silent breath.
The infant's head lolled to the side, the neck muscles offering no resistance to gravity.
Eyes remained shut, the lashes still, as if the effort to open them was too great.
A single, slow extension of the toes was the sole motor activity for over {seconds} seconds.
The body was a study in hypotonia, limbs falling open in a complete lack of postural tone.
Respiration was so minimal it failed to mist a cold stethoscope diaphragm.
Only the delicate flutter of the alae nasi indicated the work of breathing.
A profound stillness, the skin pale and cool, with capillary refill just at the threshold of normal.
The newborn lay in a state of quiet alertness, observing nothing, moving even less.
A weak suckling motion began and ended at the corner of the mouth, uncoordinated and brief.
The chest wall retracted slightly with each inspiration, a silent, shallow effort.
Limbs were pliant and heavy, draping over the supporting hand without a hint of recoil.
Eyelids opened to reveal a dull, unfocused gaze that drifted shut after a few blinks.
The infant's form seemed to sink into the bedding, a portrait of depleted energy.
A tremor passed through the lower lip, but no sound emerged, and the motion stilled.
The rooting response was a delayed, languid turn of the head after sustained stimulation.
Breath sounds were vesicular but distant, as if originating from a deep, quiet place.
A subtle cyanotic hue lingered around the mouth, fading with the first few weak cries.
Muscle tone was so reduced the infant resembled a softly filled sack of grain.
The only movement was the slow, passive rise of the abdomen with diaphragmatic breathing.
The startle reflex produced a slight jerk of one arm, then immediate, total relaxation.
Eyes rolled slowly beneath closed lids, but the body remained utterly motionless.
A sigh escaped, a small puff of air that seemed to expend the last of the baby's vigor.
The fontanelle was flat and soft, pulsing with a slow, metronomic rhythm.
The infant accepted tactile stimulation with a blink and a slight, yielding push into the touch.
Respiration was agonal in pattern, with long pauses punctuated by a single shallow breath.
The Moro response was a feeble, half-complete abduction of the arms that lacked any cry.
A veneer of stillness lay over the baby, broken only by the occasional, slow blink of a heavy lid.
